title: Guitar years with Kid Thomas at Speck's and Foster Lewis
summary: After taking up guitar he played small outfits, then two or three years with Kid Thomas at Speck's, an eleven-piece band during wartime.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Yeah, it has that drum head on it. Mm-hmm. That's right. After you took up the guitar, do you remember which bands you played with? That was in the 30s, was it?
After I took up the guitar? Mm-hmm. After I took up the guitar, well, I played with different outfits. Oh, yeah. Just small outfits, you know. Nothing much to talk about.
Was there any especially famous bands or musicians you played with after you left? Chris Kelly and Kid René and those people?
No, in the morning, I played with Kit Thomas for about two or three years.
I didn't know you were in that long, right?
With Kit Thomas.
Is that across the river, most of them?
With Speck and Long Road.
With Specks and all?
That's right.
I used to go to Specks.
I was playing guitar there. Yeah. We had 11 pieces there during wartime.
Well, a big band there.
Big place. Yeah, that's right. Needs a big band.
Yeah, that's right. Any other bands around that time that you might have worked with?
Well, you mean after Kit Thomas?
Well, yes, or even before that we might have missed.
After Kit Thomas, well, I joined in with Foster Lewis' band. Foster Lewis.
Foster Lewis, yes.
Yeah.
I've heard of him but don't know him.
Now you're talking about a trombone player. That's a sweet trombone player. Very sweet.
